newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks stay up despite bank selloff.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks stay up despite bank selloff.

text.p: Australian stocks ended slightly up on Tuesday despite a sell-off in bank shares as investors trod cautiously ahead of the Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) in the United States later today.

By 4.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 1.3 points up at 2,403.4 and about 16 points off its morning high. The share price index futures contract was eight points down at 2,382, creating a 21.4 point discount to the physical index.
Brokers said the market has already factored in a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates after the FOMC meeting and would only react tomorrow if the move any different to that.
"It started strongly on the back of the Dow, but fizzled with the banks falling away," said Richard Nelson, a fund manager at BNP Investment Management.
Bank shares boosted the market at the opening but by the end all of the "big four" banks were down.

Brokers said the turnaround in the bank shares was due to the announcement by the Treasurer Peter Costello that the government's report into the financial sector would be released in the week starting April 7.
The market had been speculating on an imminent release of the report, known as the Wallis Inquiry.
Despite the bank sell-off, the insurance sector remained buoyant, with the insurance index up over two percent. The Wallis Inquiry also covers the insurance sector.
Brokers said there was some switching into insurers from banks, as the banks have had strong gains recently.
The market was also weighted down by weaker resource stocks due to a fall in base metal prices and the bullion price.
The transport sector was also an early star on the local bourse, but also fell away as investors started to cash in their gains, brokers said.

Brokers said the fall in the share futures price contract to a 21.4 point discount just ahead of Thursday's expiry, when the contract is to run close to parity to the physical, is an indication that the physical market may weaken tomorrow.
In other local markets, Australian bonds failed to make much more headway after an intial U.S. led rally. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were yielding 7.98 percent.
The Australian dollar remained supported ahead of a meeting by the policy setting U.S. FOMC. At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7885/90 from Monday's close of US$0.7864/69.
